articles.fullText:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent walks to speak to the rest of the media outside the West Wing of the White House in Washington, DC, US, August 20 2026. 
The US threatened Iran with what it called "the greatest financial offensive ever marshalled" as it prepared to roll out economic sanctions on Monday that target Iran's trade partners.
The US Treasury is expected to broaden the scope of secondary sanctions on entities and countries that maintain business ties with Iran, a source familiar with the plans told Reuters on Monday. The move is aimed at giving countries a final warning to sever their business ties with Iran as Washington seeks to increase economic pressure on Tehran.
The source said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent would also make clear that countries continuing to do business with Iran could risk having key companies and entities cut off from the dollar-based financial system.
Iran in turn vowed to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf "if the economic war continues."
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will hold a press conference at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday amid promises to reveal even more severe measures on a country that has endured near-continuous economic sanctions since the Islamic Revolution of 1979.
"At dawn begins an economic D-Day – the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary," Bessent wrote in an opinion piece published in the Financial Times on Sunday.
Without detailing specific measures, the US treasury secretary signaled the US would target "fearful nations" that practice "appeasement" by engaging with Iran's economy and financial system.
"They would do well to consider the consequences of sustaining it," Bessent wrote in the Financial Times.
A defiant Iran
Iran has been bracing for the sanctions for days, issuing a series of strongly worded statements suggesting it planned a major military response.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, on Sunday suggested economic retaliation.
"If the economic war continues, not a single drop of oil will be exported, neither through the Strait of Hormuz nor from anywhere in the Persian Gulf," Rezaei wrote in a social media post. "Iran will regard any country's participation in or support for America's economic war against the Iranian people as an act of war."
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi dismissed the threat of new US sanctions as a sign of desperation on Sunday and said the expected new measures would fail to defeat Tehran.
"The fact that they (US leaders) have moved on from military operations to bring up the same old plans (economic sanctions) shows that they are desperate," Araqchi said in a post on Telegram.
"We have never been afraid. All of their actions – whether blockades or other military moves they have made – have failed, and this new issue of theirs will fail as well," he said.
Vessels are seen in the Strait of Hormuz, off the port city of Bandar Abbas in southern Iran, August 10, 2026. 
Strait of Hormuz nears a standstill
Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has come to an almost complete standstill amid escalating tensions.
US Central Command said the guided-missile destroyer USS John Finn had redirected 70 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two as part of efforts to enforce a US naval blockade of Iran.
Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA), the body responsible for maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, announced on Sunday in a post on X that vessels violating Iranian protocols for transiting the waterway will face restrictions on their future passages.
The PGSA called on "cargo owners shipping to and from the Persian Gulf" to review the list of "Non-Compliant Vessels" on its website prior to chartering to avoid potential issues.
Meanwhile, Hassan Qashqavi, spokesperson of the Iranian parliament's national security and foreign policy committee, said on Sunday that the committee has approved an article of a draft plan aimed at safeguarding security in the strait, under which the country will charge fees for the services it provides in the waterway, according to the semi-official Fars news agency.
Fewer than 20 commodity vessels transited the strait at the weekend, shipping data showed on Monday. Four vessels crossed the strait on Sunday and 13 on Saturday, initial data from shiptracker Kpler showed. 
Uncertain diplomatic future
With official face-to-face talks between the United States and Iran still suspended since they last met in Switzerland in June, other countries, including Qatar and Pakistan, have sought to revive diplomatic efforts.
Iran said Pakistan's army chief, Asim Munir, will visit Tehran on Monday as part of efforts to restore peace and security in the region, but offered few details.
Pakistan has been mediating in the conflict and a Pakistani government source said Munir would touch on recent developments including the US threat of new sanctions.
The imminent sanctions have also cast doubt on the prospects for diplomacy, as analysts warned that Washington's pressure campaign could ultimately prove counterproductive.
Li Zixin, a Middle East expert at the China Institute of International Studies, said although Iran would face significant economic pain, the impact would not necessarily translate into political capitulation, in an interview with China Media Group (CMG).
However, for the US itself, the backlash from sanctions cannot be ignored, Li said, adding that the average price of regular gasoline across the country is currently about 50% higher than before the war, while pressure from imported inflation is also mounting. The resulting increase in household costs will directly affect ordinary Americans.
In Li's view, the harsher the US sanctions become, the more Iran's hardliners are likely to gain the upper hand, further narrowing the space for diplomacy.
This could create a vicious cycle of "sanctions, countermeasures, and further sanctions," Li said, ultimately leaving neither side a winner.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Saturday that Canada was "at war" over trade with the United States and that, starting September 8, the country would impose tariffs on imports of US steel, electronics and other products in retaliation for US President Donald Trump's new 50% tariffs that took effect at midnight.

After days of intense negotiations, Canada and the US did not reach a trade deal late on Friday, worsening a delicate relationship between the long-term trade partners and allies, and complicating the future of the North American free trade pact involving the pair and Mexico.
Trump's new tariffs hit sectors including wine, furniture, dairy products, cement, clothing, fishing rods and hockey equipment, and cover some $20 billion of Canadian exports to the US. These duties do not exempt Canadian products under the continental trade agreement, which had shielded most Canadian exports to the US in the last 18 months.
While outlining Canada's position after trade talks with the US broke down, Carney said the Canadian counter-tariffs will cover a wide range of sectors, including dairy, steel, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, along with some sectors the US previously targeted in Canada. The government will release details over the next several days, he added.
Explaining why negotiations broke down at the last minute, Carney said that while both sides were close to a mutually beneficial agreement earlier this week, the US side introduced last-minute changes that were "unfair, uneconomic and called into question the reliability of any deal."
"We cannot accept what they have offered, and we will not give what they have asked," Carney said.
The US side's repeated disregard for existing free trade agreements such as the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) sends a bad signal to international businesses and is "certainly not good news" for renewing the agreement in the future, Carney warned.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told Fox News on Saturday that no new talks are planned with Canada.

The rift comes as the United States, Mexico and Canada are trying to renew CUSMA, a trade agreement that Trump negotiated in his first term and once praised as a triumph.
The United States has begun formal talks with Mexico to revamp the agreement, but talks with Canada have not yet begun.
CUSMA is a trilateral trade pact that replaced the North American Free Trade Agreement when it took effect on July 1, 2020. On July 1, 2026, the United States officially declined to renew the agreement for another 16-year term, triggering an annual review process until the pact expires in 2036.
A sign marking the international border between the United States and Canada is pictured at Peace Arch Historical State Park in Blaine, Washington State, US, March 5, 2025.

Carney is one of the few global leaders to retaliate against US tariffs and has pledged to forge new trade and military alliances, despite Canada's dependence on the United States for nearly 70% of its exports.
Beyond the latest tariffs, relations between Canada and the US have suffered from Trump's repeated threats to make Canada the 51st US state.
The US president was also irked by Carney's widely touted January speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, in which the Canadian prime minister declared that the global order was experiencing a "rupture."
The Canadian leader has repeatedly said that relations with the US have been forever changed and that the country must reduce its reliance on its southern neighbor.
"We've been under no illusions. We recognized from the start that America has changed," Carney told reporters on Saturday.
Wang Ruibin, director of the Department of World Economics and Development at China Institute of International Studies, said the latest tit-for-tat tariffs between the US and Canada will carry a political impact that outweighs the economic one, particularly as political trust between the two countries has already been eroded.
"A series of US actions have repeatedly exposed its unreliability as an ally, a close neighbor, and a key trading partner to Canada, dealing a blow to the very foundation of what is often described as the world's closest bilateral economic and security relationship," Wang told China Media Group.

The system, which includes three robotic arms that can hold surgical equipment, is controlled using an {{5}} 3D headset and a video-game-like {{6}}.

The {{8}} of robotic-assisted surgery should mean shorter hospital stays and quicker recovery times, which will take {{9}} off a {{10}} health service with year-long waitlists, workforce shortages and discharge {{11}}. The UK government has announced plans to invest more in robotic equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of keyhole surgeries carried out in England by 2035.
The government highlighted robotics as one of five "big bets" in a 10-year health plan for England, alongside other transformative technologies: data, AI, genomics and wearables.
Surgeons and nurses using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing surgery, at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
At St Bartholomew's Hospital in central London, visiting surgeons are among the first to be trained to use the new da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, made by US company Initiative. The system, which includes three robotic arms that can hold surgical equipment, is controlled using an immersive 3D headset and a video-game-like console.
Robotic surgical systems like this can be used across a range of specialties including urology, gynecology, abdominal, colorectal, and thoracic or general surgery.
Sasha Stamenkovic (C) using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing lung cancer surgery as Ali Ansaripour (R), senior cardiothoracic trainee on a robotic fellowship, looks on. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
The precision of robotic-assisted surgery should mean shorter hospital stays and quicker recovery times, which will take strain off a struggling health service with year-long waitlists, workforce shortages and discharge bottlenecks.
"The ability to have lots of integrated computer-aided technology on top" of human-controlled robotics "makes this precise surgery. It makes it safe surgery," says Sasha Stamenkovic, Director of Robotic Surgery and Research at Barts Health NHS Trust.
As well as improving recovery times, the greater precision also reduces the risk of complications like air leaks, a common cause of longer hospital stays following lung surgery.
Nurses assisting in lung cancer surgery using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, at St Bartholomew's Hospital. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
Ian Macleod was the first patient in Britain's NHS to undergo lung cancer surgery using the new da Vinci robotic system. Macleod says he "didn't realize" until he was wearing a surgical gown and anesthetised that he would hold this groundbreaking title, but the news "didn't faze" the 76-year-old retired detective.
Thirty minutes after the robotic-assisted operation, Macleod was back on his feet. "It was extraordinary," he says. "In fact, after the operation, I found out quite quickly that I only had one stitch." He had undergone non-robotic keyhole surgery for a different cancer in the past, and says the recovery time was "much longer". This time, he was driving his wife to the garden centrer for coffee less than a week later.
Stamenkovic runs fellowships at St Bartholomew's training surgeons on this new technology. He says it is the young surgeons who pick up the new robotic control system the fastest and who become the most adept.
"They've come with different skill sets," he says, "they've probably come with gaming skill sets, some of them have come with a musical background."
Laying out his long-term mission, Stamenkovic added: "All we need to do is harness their energy, their passion, their skill set, and teach them the right moves. And that will make the surgeon of the future."

英国政府宣布计划增加对英格兰医院机器人设备的投资，并设定目标，到2035年，英格兰90%的微创手术将使用机器人辅助。政府将机器人技术列为英格兰十年健康计划中的五大“重大赌注”之一，其他变革性技术包括数据、人工智能、基因组学和可穿戴设备。外科医生和护士在伦敦圣巴塞洛缪医院使用新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

在伦敦市中心的圣巴塞洛缪医院，来访的外科医生是首批接受使用新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统培训的人员之一，该系统由美国公司Initiative制造。该系统包括三个可持手术器械的机械臂，通过沉浸式3D头戴设备和类似视频游戏的控制台进行操作。

此类机器人手术系统可应用于多个专科，包括泌尿科、妇科、腹部、结直肠、胸腔或普通外科。Sasha Stamenkovic（中）使用新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行肺癌手术，Ali Ansaripour（右）是机器人专科的高级心胸外科培训生，正在观摩。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

机器人辅助手术的精准性应能缩短住院时间并加快康复速度，这将缓解医疗服务的压力，该系统目前面临长达一年的等待名单、劳动力短缺和出院瓶颈。“在人类控制的机器人技术之上集成大量计算机辅助技术的能力，使这种手术精准。它使手术安全，”巴特斯健康NHS信托机器人手术与研究主任Sasha Stamenkovic说。

除了改善康复时间，更高的精准度还降低了并发症的风险，如空气泄漏，这是肺手术后住院时间延长的常见原因。护士在圣巴塞洛缪医院使用新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统协助肺癌手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

Ian Macleod是英国NHS中第一位使用新型达芬奇机器人系统进行肺癌手术的患者。Macleod说，直到他穿上手术服并被麻醉，他才“意识到”自己将拥有这一开创性的头衔，但这一消息“没有吓到”这位76岁的退休侦探。机器人辅助手术后三十分钟，Macleod就重新站了起来。

“这太不寻常了，”他说。“事实上，手术后，我很快发现我只有一针缝合。”他过去曾因另一种癌症接受过非机器人微创手术，并表示恢复时间“长得多”。这次，不到一周后，他就开车带妻子去花园中心喝咖啡。Stamenkovic在圣巴塞洛缪医院举办奖学金项目，培训外科医生使用这项新技术。他说，年轻外科医生掌握新机器人控制系统最快，也最熟练。

“他们带来了不同的技能组合，”他说，“他们可能带来了游戏技能，有些人有音乐背景。”

在阐述其长期使命时，Stamenkovic补充道：“我们只需要利用他们的精力、热情和技能，教他们正确的动作。这将造就未来的外科医生。”

articles.fullText:
Europe is experiencing a summer of extreme heat and drought, with record temperatures, wildfire risks and falling river levels affecting several countries.
A scorched landscape in the wake of a wildfire that swept through the Gironde region in Lege-Cap-Ferret, southwestern France, August 4, 2026. 
France recorded its hottest July since nationwide records began in 1900, with a monthly average temperature of 24.9 degrees Celsius, according to Meteo-France.
Rainfall across the country was nearly 70% below the seasonal average, making July 2026 the third-driest July on record.
Persistent heat, drought and windy conditions kept wildfire risks high or very high, while a wildfire in the southwestern department of Gironde burned about 42,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of more than 220,000 people.
Boats lie in the dried out riverbed of a branch of the river Danube in Hainburg, Austria, August 3, 2026. 
In Austria, a national temperature record of 41 degrees Celsius was set on Tuesday as the heat wave continued. The record was measured in the Stammersdorf region of Vienna, according to Austria's state broadcaster ORF.
A forest fire is also raging in Burgenland, while the Lobau wetlands in Vienna face the highest fire danger level. Meanwhile, water levels on the Danube River have fallen to historically low levels, comparable to the major low-water years of 2003 and 2018.
The dried-up Danube riverbed with the Paks power plant at the background, near Dunaszentbenedek, close to Paks town, Hungary, July 31, 2026. 
Neighboring Hungary has extended its highest-level heat alert until midnight on Friday as forecasts show the heat wave will continue. Authorities warned that persistent high temperatures could affect everyone and urged people to take precautions.
The heat wave has intensified drought conditions, lowered water levels in major rivers and increased wildfire risks, with firefighters recently responding to around 100 outdoor fires per day.
A firefighting helicopter flies toward a wildfire on a mountain near L'Aquila, central Italy, August 3, 2026. 
Italy is also facing its fourth major heat wave of the summer, with temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius in some areas.
The Health Ministry placed 25 of the country's 27 monitored cities under the highest heat alert, including Rome, Milan, Florence, Bologna, Venice, Naples and Palermo.
Hot and dry conditions have increased wildfire risks and put pressure on agriculture, with farmers reporting reduced crop yields and higher irrigation demand.
A general view of the Paks nuclear power plant, Hungary, July 31, 2026. 
Low river levels and rising water temperatures have also affected nuclear power operations in parts of Europe.
Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant, which supplies nearly half of the country's electricity, remained operational but its operation depended on river conditions and cooling system performance.
Romania's Cernavoda nuclear power plant shut down both reactors after low Danube water levels affected operations. In France and Switzerland, some nuclear facilities also faced operational disruptions as high river temperatures affected cooling capacity.
The combination of extreme heat, drought and declining water availability is putting pressure on public health, agriculture, wildfire prevention and energy systems in affected areas.

APEC economies should step up efforts to eliminate trade barriers and take more concrete measures to address cross-border trade bottlenecks so as to make supply chains in the Asia-Pacific region safer, more stable and more efficient, a Chinese customs official said on Saturday.
"Security and facilitation are eternal themes of customs governance," Zhang Baofeng, deputy chief of the General Administration of Customs, said at the ongoing second plenary meeting of the 2026 APEC Sub-Committee on Customs Procedures (SCCP) in Dalian, northeast China's Liaoning Province.
Amid growing fragmentation of global supply chains, adjusting rules and standards and strengthening supply chain resilience have never been more urgent, Zhang noted.
He expressed hope that all parties will take the meeting as an opportunity to deepen alignment of rules and standards, strengthen coordination on risk management and supervision, reduce transaction costs, improve customs clearance efficiency and provide businesses with a safer, more transparent and more predictable business environment.
The Asia-Pacific region, home to one-third of the world's population, accounts for over 60% of the global economy and nearly half of global trade, serving as a key engine of global economic growth.
China's trade with other APEC economies totaled 18 trillion yuan (about $2.65 trillion) in the first seven months of this year, up 21% year on year, outpacing overall growth in China's foreign trade in goods and demonstrating strong potential for regional cooperation.
During the meeting, participants observed smart devices, exchanged experience and ideas and built consensus. China's customs shared the latest progress of the smart customs partnership program and held an exhibition showcasing achievements in smart customs development.
Zhang also put forward a three-point proposal to further deepen APEC customs cooperation – upholding true multilateralism and jointly building a new pattern of open and inclusive Asia-Pacific cooperation; riding the wave of the digital era and reshaping new paradigms of customs governance with technological innovation; balancing security and facilitation; and underpinning lasting prosperity in the Asia-Pacific region with a resilient and stable supply chain system.
The meeting also approved an APEC customs cooperation document on promoting technology and innovation for trade security and facilitation.
The APEC SCCP was established in 1994. China's customs holds the SCCP chairmanship for 2026. This meeting, following the first plenary in Guangzhou in February this year, featured in-depth discussions on cutting-edge topics such as artificial intelligence, smart customs and cross-border e-commerce.
